atoms.obligation: Work the required sections in order, treating each one as an obligation you can be held to.
atoms.lesson: This skill guides the analyst through a validation end to end. Work the sections in order; each one names an obligation you can be held to.

atoms.obligation: Structure the report to state the quantity, the reference, stratified agreement, failure cases and the domain of validity.
atoms.lesson:
The analyst owns this step.

Structure the validation as: definition of the quantity, reference data and why it is a fair reference, agreement statistics stratified by the dimensions that matter (season, geography, magnitude), failure cases shown rather than described, and a stated domain of validity. A validation that reports only pooled agreement hides exactly the regimes where the indicator fails.
atoms.anchor: 1. Validation report structure for a derived indicator

atoms.obligation: Stop and escalate whenever you cannot satisfy this requirement rather than proceeding.
atoms.lesson: Section 1 (Validation report structure for a derived indicator) ends with: "If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate." The structure obligation is not optional — if the definition of the quantity, a fair reference, stratified agreement statistics, shown failure cases or a stated domain of validity cannot be produced, the validation does not proceed; it goes back up.
atoms.anchor: 1. Validation report structure for a derived indicator

atoms.obligation: State the measurement units, reference frame and time basis on every numeric field and every chart axis.
atoms.lesson:
Skipping this is the most common way a validation goes wrong.

State units, coordinate reference system and time zone on every numeric column and every chart axis. Default to SI units, EPSG:4326 for lon/lat storage, an equal- area projection for any area computation, and UTC for all timestamps.
atoms.anchor: 2. Be explicit about units, CRS and time zones

atoms.obligation: Convert values to local conventions only at the presentation layer, never in storage.
atoms.lesson: Convert to local conventions only at the presentation layer, never in storage. Storage stays on the defaults: SI units, EPSG:4326 for lon/lat, an equal- area projection for any area computation, and UTC for all timestamps.
atoms.anchor: 2. Be explicit about units, CRS and time zones

atoms.obligation: Record the outcome of this step in the working notes.
atoms.lesson: Section 2 (Be explicit about units, CRS and time zones) ends with: "Record the outcome of this step in the validation notes." The declared units, coordinate reference system and time zone conventions must be written into the validation notes, not merely applied.
atoms.anchor: 2. Be explicit about units, CRS and time zones

atoms.obligation: Before claiming a change is real, confirm it exceeds the noise floor of the measurement.
atoms.lesson:
Apply this before the validation leaves your hands.

Before claiming a change is real, check that it exceeds the noise floor: compute the metric's run-to-run variance, use a paired comparison where the same units appear in both arms, and require the effect to survive a simple resampling test.

atoms.obligation: Report the sample size alongside any average, never the average alone.
atoms.lesson: Report the number of units, not just the mean. A mean reported without the number of units behind it invites over-reading a difference that the run-to-run variance, the paired comparison and the resampling test would not support.

atoms.obligation: Record the outcome of this step in the working notes.
atoms.lesson: Section 3 (Do not over-read small differences) ends with: "Record the outcome of this step in the validation notes." The noise-floor check — run-to-run variance, the paired comparison, the resampling test and the number of units — is written into the validation notes.

atoms.obligation: For every result, capture the inputs, versions, time window, code revision and configuration used to produce it.
atoms.lesson:
This section applies to every validation without exception.

Nothing ships without lineage. For each result, capture the upstream dataset IDs and their versions, the time window covered, the commit SHA of the code that ran, and a hash of the run configuration.

atoms.obligation: Keep the provenance record co-located with the output it describes.
atoms.lesson: Keep that record co-located with the artefact itself. An artefact whose origin cannot be reconstructed is not a deliverable. Nothing ships without lineage, and this section applies to every validation without exception.

atoms.obligation: Track quality and coverage per derived value, exclude values failing the threshold, and label anything you filled in.
atoms.lesson:
Apply this before the validation leaves your hands.

A missing observation is not a zero. Track observation count and cloud fraction per derived value, drop scenes exceeding the cloud threshold, and label any gap-fill you perform. Coverage is a headline metric.

atoms.obligation: Stop and escalate whenever you cannot satisfy this requirement rather than proceeding.
atoms.lesson: Section 5 (Cloud mask: what is required) ends with: "If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate." If observation count and cloud fraction cannot be tracked per derived value, if scenes over the cloud threshold cannot be dropped, or if gap-fill cannot be labelled, the validation stops here rather than silently treating a missing observation as a zero.

atoms.obligation: Attach an uncertainty range to every point estimate, stating what it covers, what it excludes and the dominant term.
atoms.lesson: Point estimates travel with an uncertainty band and a note on what the band covers and excludes, plus the dominant error term. This section is marked non-negotiable.

atoms.obligation: Disclose uncertainty you cannot quantify in words rather than omitting it.
atoms.lesson: Unquantifiable uncertainty is disclosed in words, not omitted. Omission reads as confidence the work does not have; the disclosure sits alongside the uncertainty band and the dominant error term.

atoms.obligation: Set a time budget for investigation before starting and escalate the moment it expires.
atoms.lesson: Set the investigation budget before you start and escalate when it expires, even mid- thought. The budget is set in advance precisely so that the decision to escalate is not made by someone who is already deep in the problem.
atoms.anchor: 7. Time-box investigation and escalate on the clock

atoms.obligation: When escalating, state what you tried, what you ruled out and what you would try next.
atoms.lesson: State what you tried, what you ruled out and what you would try next — an escalation with those three things costs the next person minutes, not hours.
atoms.anchor: 7. Time-box investigation and escalate on the clock

atoms.obligation: Produce a record sufficient for someone else to reproduce the run independently.
atoms.lesson: Produce a manifest sufficient for an independent re-run: invocation command, image digest, locked dependency set, seeds, and run window.

atoms.obligation: Prove the reproduction record works by running it once in a clean environment before relying on it.
atoms.lesson: Prove it works by executing it once in a fresh environment; an unverified manifest is a guess. The manifest — invocation command, image digest, locked dependency set, seeds, and run window — is only evidence of reproducibility once it has actually been re-run.

atoms.obligation: Maintain a visible list of assumptions and open questions, each with an owner and the cost of being wrong.
atoms.lesson: Keep a visible list of the assumptions the work rests on and the questions still open, each with the person who can settle it and the cost of being wrong. Assumptions that nobody owns are the ones that fail silently.

atoms.obligation: Stop and escalate whenever you cannot satisfy this requirement rather than proceeding.
atoms.lesson: Section 9 (Surface assumptions and open questions) ends with: "If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate." If the assumptions and open questions cannot be listed visibly, or no person can be named against each one with the cost of being wrong, that is itself the escalation — unowned assumptions fail silently.

atoms.obligation: Keep a small frozen set of known-correct cases versioned with the code and compare against it on every change.
atoms.lesson:
Apply this before the validation leaves your hands.

Keep a small frozen set of cases with known-correct outputs, versioned with the code, and diff against it on every change.
atoms.anchor: 10. Validate against a frozen golden set for this validation

atoms.obligation: When an expected result legitimately changes, update it in its own change with the reason recorded.
atoms.lesson: When a golden case legitimately changes, update it in its own commit with the reason in the message — never in the same commit as the behaviour change. Mixing the two makes it impossible to tell an intended update from a regression that was blessed by accident.
atoms.anchor: 10. Validate against a frozen golden set for this validation

atoms.obligation: Record the outcome of this step in the working notes.
atoms.lesson: Section 10 (Validate against a frozen golden set for this validation) ends with: "Record the outcome of this step in the validation notes." The result of diffing against the frozen golden set, and any golden case updated, is written into the validation notes.
atoms.anchor: 10. Validate against a frozen golden set for this validation

atoms.obligation: Confirm every required step is complete against the closing checklist before the work leaves your hands.
atoms.lesson:
The document closes with a checklist covering every section:

- [ ] Validation report structure for a derived indicator
- [ ] Be explicit about units, CRS and time zones
- [ ] Do not over-read small differences
- [ ] Record provenance and lineage
- [ ] Handle cloud cover and missing observations
- [ ] Report uncertainty honestly
- [ ] Time-box investigation and escalate on the clock
- [ ] Emit a reproducibility manifest
- [ ] Surface assumptions and open questions
- [ ] Validate against a frozen golden set
